actions.name: conducted credential stuffing attacks against US financial institutions
actions.description: Since 2017, the FBI has received numerous reports on credential stuffing attacks against US financial institutions, collectively detailing nearly 50,000 account compromises.

actions.name: masqueraded as legitimate account holders and bank employees to submit fraudulent transactions
actions.description: The attackers masqueraded as legitimate account holders and bank employees to submit fraudulent transactions, including money transfers, bill payments, and credit card reward points purchases.

actions.name: used botnets to conduct massive scale automated login attempts
actions.description: Cyber actors used botnets to conduct a massive scale of automated login attempts in a short timeframe enabling them to discover multiple valid credential pairs.

actions.name: targeted application programming interfaces (APIs) in credential stuffing attacks
actions.description: Between May and September 2019, as much as 75 percent of credential stuffing attacks against the financial industry targeted APIs.

actions.name: used aggregation software to link actor-controlled accounts to client accounts
actions.description: Between January and August 2020, unidentified actors used aggregation software to link actor-controlled accounts to client accounts belonging to the same institution, resulting in more than $3.5 million in fraudulent check withdrawals and ACH transfers.

actions.name: conducted credential stuffing attacks against mobile APIs of financial firms
actions.description: Between June 2019 and January 2020, a NY-based investment firm and an international money transfer platform experienced credential stuffing attacks against their mobile APIs.

actions.name: caused extended system outage preventing revenue collection
actions.description: One of the credential stuffing attacks resulted in an extended system outage that prevented the collection of nearly $2 million in revenue.

actions.name: compromised more than 4,000 online banking accounts
actions.description: Between June and November 2019, a small group of cyber criminals targeted a financial services institution and three of its clients, resulting in the compromise of more than 4,000 online banking accounts.

actions.name: submitted fraudulent payments using bill payment services
actions.description: The cyber criminals used bill payment services to submit fraudulent payments—about $40,000 in total—to themselves, which they then wired to foreign banking accounts.
